newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilgener opens bidding for power lines.
newsitem.headline: Chilgener opens bidding for power lines.

text.p: Chilean power generator Chilgener has opened bidding for contracts to build a 263 kilometer(km) power transmission line from the northern Argentine city of Salta to the Chilean border, the company said.
The call for bids was made through Chilgener's Argentine subsidiary TermoAndes SA, said Chilgener in a statement.
The company will at some later stage call for bids to build the Chilean segment of the 408 km, trans-Andean power transmission line known as ElectroAndes, due to come onstream in late 1998.
Chilgener took a swipe at the Atacama project led by competitor Endesa and CMS Energy Corp to build a natural gas pipeline over the Andes from Salta to northern Chile.

Without mentioning either company by name, Chilgener said the natural gas project had been "unanimously discarded because it yields economic results inferior to those of the solution under development."
On Wednesday, Chilean power utility Empresa Electrica del Norte Grande SA (Eldenor) said in a statement it plans to buy gas from the Atacama pipeline.

However, Edelnor, controlled by Atlanta-based Southern Co and Atacama's first major client, cautioned that it "remains to be demonstrated" that the Atacama pipeline is "viable given current demand levels and the distance that the pipeline will have to cover from northern Argentina to the coast of Chile."
Both projects aim to supply power to northern Chile, center of the country's booming copper industry, and have begun competing for clients.
Construction of the Argentine sector of the power lines calls for participation by 18 companies. They have until March 17 to present their bids, said Chilgener.

Chilgener's project includes construction of a 600 MW power plant in Salta, with an investment of $210 million, plus the power lines over the Andes to be connected to southern end of the northern Chile power grid known by its Spanish acronym SING.

Chilgener already has 110 MW of its production committed to two big copper mining companies, Zaldivar and Gibraltar, and the rest will be sold to other clients on the SING, said Chilgener's statement.
